questions.q: Benzenediazonium chloride is warmed with copper powder and HBr. The product is:
questions.explain: Cu powder with HX on a diazonium salt is the Gattermann reaction, which replaces –N₂⁺ by Cl or Br with loss of N₂. Phenol would form on warming in water alone.

questions.q: Which statement correctly compares the Gattermann and Sandmeyer reactions?
options: Gattermann uses CuCl; Sandmeyer uses copper powder
Gattermann uses copper powder and generally gives lower yields than Sandmeyer
Gattermann goes through an aryl cation, Sandmeyer through an aryl radical
questions.explain: Gattermann uses metallic Cu with HX; Sandmeyer uses a copper(I) salt and gives the better yield. Copper powder works through Cu⁺ formed in situ, so both go via an aryl radical.

questions.q: Which compound CANNOT be prepared from the corresponding diazonium salt by the Gattermann reaction?
questions.explain: The Gattermann reaction introduces only Cl and Br. Cyanide is introduced with CuCN (Sandmeyer), iodide with KI and fluoride by the Balz–Schiemann reaction.

questions.q: p-Toluidine is converted into compound X with NaNO₂/HCl at 273–278 K, and X is warmed with Cu/HBr to give Y. Y is:
questions.explain: Diazotisation gives p-toluenediazonium chloride (X), and the Gattermann reaction replaces –N₂⁺ by Br at the same position. The amino group fixes the position of the halogen before it is removed.
